title: Conormal and strict-transform geometry for a regular flag
statement:
Let $Z\xrightarrow{i}Y\xrightarrow{j}X$ be regular closed immersions of Noetherian schemes of constant codimensions $m,n>0$. Regular means locally cut out by a regular sequence [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Write $N_{X/Y}=I_Y/I_Y^2$ for the conormal module, and similarly for other immersions. For every regular closed immersion $W\hookrightarrow V$ of Noetherian schemes of constant codimension $c\geq0$ (a single one, not necessarily part of a flag), its conormal module is finite locally free of rank $c$ [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]; in particular the conormal modules of $i$, $j$ and $ji$ are finite locally free of ranks $m$, $n$ and $m+n$. Their natural sequence is exact:
$$0\to i^*N_{X/Y}\to N_{X/Z}\to N_{Y/Z}\to0.$$
Write $\operatorname{Bl}_W V=\operatorname{Proj}_V\bigoplus_{a\geq0}I_W^a$ and $P(F)=\operatorname{Proj}(\operatorname{Sym}F)$ [def-nagata-relative-proj]. For $\pi:B=\operatorname{Bl}_Y X\to X$, the exceptional subscheme is $P=P(N_{X/Y})$, an effective Cartier divisor, with $\mathcal I_P=\mathcal O_B(1)$ [def-nagata-effective-cartier-ideal]. Put $P'=P\times_Y Z$ and let $p:P\to Y$, $p':P'\to Z$, $i':P'\hookrightarrow P$, $j':P\hookrightarrow B$. Then $i'$ has codimension $m$ and $j'i'$ codimension $m+1$. The natural conormal maps give surjections
$$p^*N_{X/Y}\twoheadrightarrow N_{B/P},\qquad p'^*N_{X/Z}\twoheadrightarrow N_{B/P'}.$$
Their kernels $K$ and $K'$ are vector bundles of rank $n-1$, with the canonical isomorphism $i'^*K\cong K'$. The conormal of $i'$ identifies with $p'^*N_{Y/Z}$.
If $n=1$, instead take $\pi:B=\operatorname{Bl}_Z X\to X$, let $P=P(N_{X/Z})$ be its exceptional divisor, and let $\widetilde Y=\operatorname{Bl}_Z Y$ be the strict transform of $Y$. Then $\widetilde Y\hookrightarrow B$ is an effective Cartier divisor, $P'=P(N_{Y/Z})=P\cap\widetilde Y$, and $P$ and $\widetilde Y$ meet transversely (their intersection is an effective Cartier divisor on each). If $I=\mathcal I_Y$, then
$$\pi^*I\cong\mathcal I_P\otimes\mathcal I_{\widetilde Y}$$
as invertible modules with their canonical trivializations off $\pi^{-1}Y$. Put $K_0=i^*N_{X/Y}$, a line on $Z$. The ideal of $P'\subset P$ is $p_P^*K_0\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$, where $p_P:P\to Z$ is the projective bundle projection. No regularity of the ambient schemes is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVI, proof of Lemma 2.3.3, pp. 234-235 (conormal diagram and its kernels), and proof of Theorem 2.3.2, pp. 236-237 (strict-transform factorization and hyperplane ideal).

proof.text: For a single regular immersion $W\hookrightarrow V$, work on an affine neighbourhood on which its ideal is $J=(h_1,\ldots,h_c)$ with $h$ regular. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free], the classes $[h_1],\ldots,[h_c]$ form a basis of $J/J^2$ over $R/J$. These are local frames of the conormal sheaf, giving finite local freeness of rank $c$ by [def-amb-finite-locally-free-module]. This also covers $c=0$: the empty sequence gives $J=0$ and the zero conormal. No hypothesis that $R$ is regular is used.

source.place: XVI, 2.3.1 and proof of Lemma 2.3.3, p.234; algebra.tex Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular (degree one).

proof.text: Near a point of $Z$, choose equations $f_1,\ldots,f_n$ for $Y\subset X$ and lifts $g_1,\ldots,g_m$ of regular equations for $Z\subset Y$. Put $J=(f)$ and $H=(f,g)$ in the affine ring $R$. The concatenation $(f,g)$ is regular: the successive quotients in its first $n$ positions are those for $f$, and all later quotients are those for $\bar g$ in $R/J$; the final quotient is nonzero at the chosen point. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] to these three sequences. In their bases the natural conormal sequence is the inclusion of the $f$ coordinates followed by projection onto the $g$ coordinates. It is therefore short exact, locally split, and has ranks $n,m+n,m$. These maps are the maps induced by inclusions and quotients of ideals, so the local sequences are the stated global sequence.

source.place: XVI, proof of Lemma 2.3.3, conormal diagram p.235, and proof of Theorem 2.3.2, short exact sequence p.237.

proof.text: The chart computations below may use any chosen generator as the first member of a regular sequence. Here is the precise local justification. At a point of the relevant centre, [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-regular-sequence-localization-prime] makes the chosen sequence regular in the Noetherian local ring. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-permutation-noetherian-local] with the finite module $M=R_{\mathfrak p}$ to put the selected generator first. By [lem-exc-regular-sequence-principal-neighbourhood], shrink to a principal affine neighbourhood on which this ordering is regular. There are finitely many orderings used, so intersect these neighbourhoods when necessary. For $(f,g)$ in Step 2, apply this to the concatenated sequence over $R$ and also to $\bar g$ over $R/(f)$, which is Noetherian. Away from a centre its ideal is the unit ideal and the local blowup is the identity, since the degree-zero localization of $R[T]$ at $T$ is $R$.

source.place: XVI, pp.234-237, local regular-flag geometry; algebra.tex Tag 00LJ (lemma-permute-xi) and Tag 061L (lemma-regular-sequence-in-neighbourhood).

proof.text:
For either centre used in the statement, write its regular equations as $h_1,\ldots,h_r$ after Step 3. The opens $C_k=R[(h)/h_k]$ cover its blowup by [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover]. On such an open, [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation] gives
$$C_k=R[u_l\mid l\ne k]/(h_ku_l-h_l\mid l\ne k).$$
Write $t=h_k$ and $u_k=1$. Then $(h)C_k=(t)$. Multiplication by $t$ is injective, because [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring] realizes $C_k$ as a subring of $R_t$, where $t$ is a unit. Thus the inverse image of the centre is Cartier and
$$C_k/(t)=(R/(h))[u_l\mid l\ne k].$$
These are exactly the standard charts of $P((h)/(h)^2)$, using the conormal basis of Step 1 and the free-module case of [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. The comparison is induced by the canonical graded map from the symmetric algebra of the conormal to the associated graded: on generators it sends $[h_l]$ to its degree-one ideal class, so also commutes with changes of the regular frame. On the overlap of charts $k,q$, the coordinate change is $u_l^{(q)}=u_l^{(k)}/u_q^{(k)}$, the same fraction identity on both schemes. This proves the canonical exceptional-divisor identification for both blowups, rather than merely identifying their underlying points.

source.place: XVI, Lemma 2.3.3 p.234 and Theorem 2.3.2 p.236; more-algebra.tex Tag 0BIQ (lemma-blowup-regular-sequence); divisors.tex Tag 0804 (lemma-blowing-up-affine).

proof.text: The Cartier ideal in Step 4 is canonically $\mathcal O_B(1)$. Indeed, by [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] the degree-one twist on $D_+(h_k)$ is free with basis the degree-one homogeneous element $h_k$ of the Rees algebra: divide a degree-one fraction by $h_k$ to obtain a degree-zero fraction. Send that basis to $t\in(t)\subset C_k$. On a $k,q$ overlap the two bases have ratio $h_q/h_k=u_q^{(k)}$, exactly the ratio of the ideal generators. These isomorphisms therefore glue. The universal map from the pulled-back centre ideal sends $h_l$ to $tu_l$; after restriction to the exceptional divisor it induces the stated natural conormal map. Its target is $(t)/(t^2)$, freely generated by $[t]$.

source.place: XVI, proof of Lemma 2.3.3, pp.234-235; divisors.tex Tag 02OS (lemma-blowing-up-gives-effective-Cartier-divisor), final paragraph.

proof.text: Now use the first blowup, with centre $J=(f)$, and a chart with pivot $f_k=t$. Its exceptional chart is $(R/J)[u_l\mid l\ne k]$. The fibre product $P'$ is cut out there by $\bar g_1,\ldots,\bar g_m$, so its ring is $(R/H)[u_l\mid l\ne k]$. The sequence $\bar g$ remains regular over the polynomial ring: each successive multiplication is injective coefficient by coefficient, and its final quotient is a nonzero polynomial ring. Consequently $P'\hookrightarrow P$ is regular of codimension $m$. In $C_k$, $(t,g_1,\ldots,g_m)$ is regular, since $t$ is injective by Step 4 and the remaining sequence in $C_k/t$ is the one just checked. This proves regularity and codimension $m+1$ of $P'\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: XVI, proof of Lemma 2.3.3, p.234: codimensions of $i\prime$ and $j\prime i\prime$, with the flat-coordinate check written explicitly.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free], the conormal of $P'\hookrightarrow P$ has the basis $[g_1],\ldots,[g_m]$ on the charts in Step 6. The map from $p'^*N_{Y/Z}$ sends its basis $[\bar g_j]$ to this basis, so is an isomorphism. Because the map is induced by the ideals in the fibre-product square, these local identifications agree on overlaps and give the asserted canonical identification. The same cited basis theorem applied to $(t,g)$ makes $N_{B/P'}$ free on $[t],[g_1],\ldots,[g_m]$.

source.place: XVI, proof of Lemma 2.3.3, p.235, bottom right entry and exact conormal row.

proof.text: In the chart of Step 6 the first conormal map sends $[f_k]\mapsto[t]$ and $[f_l]\mapsto u_l[t]$ for $l\ne k$. It is onto and its kernel is free on $[f_l]-u_l[f_k]$, $l\ne k$: subtract the corresponding combination to leave only the $f_k$ coordinate. The second map, with source basis $[f_1],\ldots,[f_n],[g_1],\ldots,[g_m]$ over $\mathcal O_{P'}$, has the same $f$ formulas and sends $[g_j]\mapsto[g_j]$. Hence it is onto and its kernel has exactly the same $n-1$ basis vectors. Restricting the first kernel and then using the natural conormal map gives these identical vectors in the second kernel. This is the canonical isomorphism $i'^*K\simeq K'$; it glues because it is the restriction of the natural ideal-induced maps, and the displayed local map is an isomorphism everywhere. For $n=1$ both bases are empty, so both kernels are zero.

source.place: XVI, proof of Lemma 2.3.3, p.235, exact diagram and canonical kernel isomorphism; explicit matrices in the regular frames of Steps 1, 2 and 7.

proof.text:
For the second blowup set $n=1$, write $a=f_1$, and use the centre $H=(a,g_1,\ldots,g_m)$. The strict transform is $\operatorname{Bl}_{( ar g)}(\operatorname{Spec}(R/a))$ as a closed subscheme of $B$ by [lemma-nagata-strict-transform-ambient-closed]. In the $a$-chart it is empty: its corresponding blowup chart on $R/a$ has pivot zero and is the zero ring (the localization at zero is zero). In a $g_k$-chart put $t=g_k$, $u=a/t$ and $v_j=g_j/t$ for $j
e k$. By [lem-trf-blowup-chart-regular-sequence-presentation],
$$C=R[u,v_j\mid j
e k]/(tu-a,tv_j-g_j\mid j
e k).$$
The same presentation over $R/a$ for the regular sequence $ ar g$ identifies $C/(u)$ with the $g_k$-chart of that blowup. This quotient is the natural closed-immersion map from the cited strict-transform theorem, since it sends every fraction to its reduced fraction. Thus the strict-transform ideal is $(u)$ on these charts.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p.236, strict-transform diagram; more-algebra.tex Tag 0BIQ (lemma-blowup-regular-sequence).

proof.text:
In Step 9, $u$ is a nonzerodivisor in $C$. Indeed $a$ is a nonzerodivisor in $R$ and hence in $R_t$: if $a(b/t^d)=0$, some $t^eab=0$, whence $t^eb=0$. The chart $C$ is a subring of $R_t$, and $a=tu$ there. Thus $ux=0$ implies $ax=0$ and then $x=0$. The strict transform is consequently an effective Cartier divisor. Its intersection with $P$ has ring
$$C/(t,u)=(R/H)[v_j\mid j\ne k].$$
On $P$, the equation $u$ is a polynomial variable in $C/t=(R/H)[u,v_j]$, so is a nonzerodivisor. On the strict transform, $t$ is a nonzerodivisor in $C/u$: by Step 9 this ring is a blowup chart over $R/a$, a subring of $(R/a)_t$ where $t$ is invertible. The intersection is therefore Cartier on each divisor. On the exceptional projective bundle its equation is the homogeneous coordinate of $a$; the remaining $g$ charts give precisely $P(N_{Y/Z})$. This proves both the scheme-theoretic equality and the asserted transverse intersection, also when $m=1$.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p.236, transverse Cartier divisors and their intersection; algebra.tex lemma-affine-blowup (injectivity read directly from the chart definition).

proof.text:
Multiplication of ideal sheaves gives the required global factorization. On each $g_k$-chart its formula is
$$(t)\otimes_C(u)\longrightarrow(a),\qquad (bt)\otimes(cu)\longmapsto bc\,a,$$
since $a=tu$. Both generators are nonzerodivisors, so this sends a free rank-one basis to a free rank-one basis. The module $\pi^*I$ has basis the pullback of $a$, and its map to $(a)$ is an isomorphism by the same injectivity. On the $a$-chart the strict-transform ideal is the unit ideal, and the formula is $(a)\otimes C\simeq(a)$. These are restrictions of multiplication, so glue. Local principality by nonzerodivisors also gives invertibility by [lemma-nagata-effective-cartier-is-invertible]. Off $\pi^{-1}Y$, all these ideals are unit ideals, and multiplication sends $1\otimes1$ to $1$, proving compatibility with the canonical trivializations.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p.236, canonical isomorphism of invertible sheaves and its trivializations.

proof.text: Restrict the canonical tautological quotient on $P=P(N_{X/Z})$ from [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry] to obtain $p_P^*K_0\to\mathcal O_P(1)$; tensor with $\mathcal O_P(-1)$ to obtain a map to $\mathcal O_P$. In the frame $a$ of $K_0$, and the chart frame $g_k$ of $\mathcal O_P(1)$, this map is multiplication by $a/g_k=u$. On the $a$-chart it is multiplication by $1$. Step 10 shows its image is exactly the ideal of $P'$, and its local formulas are injective. Therefore it identifies $p_P^*K_0\otimes\mathcal O_P(-1)$ with that ideal. These formulas arise from the tautological map, so agree when the conormal frame or the projective chart changes; explicitly, changing the pivot from $h_k$ to $h_q$ multiplies the dual twist frame by $h_k/h_q$, the same factor changing $a/h_k$ to $a/h_q$. This verifies the sign of the twist and the canonicity of the isomorphism.

source.place: XVI, proof of Theorem 2.3.2, p.237, ideal of the projective hyperplane $P\prime$.

split_report.summary: Proved the full geometric statement by regular-sequence conormal bases and explicit blowup chart matrices. Reused existing conormal, permutation, neighbourhood and blowup-presentation nodes; no new nodes. Checked the ILO geometric assertions independently over singular Noetherian bases, the twist signs and both canonical maps. The statement is unchanged.
split_report.blueprint: The supporting geometry at blueprint.from.place implements the regular finite-torsion local-model input to Step 3 of lem-per-artin-gabber-affine-curve through lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus: single-immersion conormal frames, ILO XVI 2.3.3 reduction by blowing up Y, and XVI 2.3.2 divisor case by blowing up Z. Steps 1-8 realize the conormal/excess diagram; Steps 9-12 realize the strict-transform, product and hyperplane-ideal assertions. No chapter or unit route is replaced.

tool_uses.why: General commutative-algebra basis theorem for an ideal generated by a regular sequence; the perverse unit supplies no algebraic replacement.
General localization tool to apply the Noetherian local permutation theorem at points of a centre.
General algebra tool to put a chosen pivot first; used only to justify the source blowup-chart calculation.
General algebraic spreading tool to realize the permitted local reorderings on actual affine neighbourhoods.
General blowup coordinate-cover theorem needed for the ILO regular-flag geometry.
General algebra presentation of regular-sequence blowup charts, used as a black box in the ILO geometry, not as a trace-formula route.
General identification of the strict transform with the induced blowup of a closed subscheme; used in the divisor-case geometry.
General ideal-sheaf tool to read the locally computed Cartier ideals as invertible modules.
General projective-bundle tool giving the canonical quotient and the standard free-module projective charts; used to identify the local exceptional charts and the hyperplane ideal in ILO XVI.

ILO prints N_{Bl/P'} where it means N_{Bl/P}; the item uses N_{B/P}, which is correct. The 0BIQ chart presentation is applied with the pivot placed first. t is a nonzerodivisor because C_k⊂R_t, and C_k/t=(R/h)[u]. In the kernel matrices the kernel is free on e_l-u_l e_k, of rank n-1, for both maps. Small cases tested: c=0, n=1, m=n=1, m=1, and a non-reduced base. There are no new nodes and no cycle.
